commits.subject: mn_petition_15218-set: ten statutory grounds stop being one empty sentence

theHEADLINE: Ten EXP102 item 9 boxes, each swearing to a DIFFERENT statutory ground for expungement, were delivered with reason: null in both records, named in neither guide, and covered by one sentence telling the participant they were his -- on a petition signed under Minn. Stat. Sec 358.116. None of the ten is ticked and none will be: the election is the participant's oath. Each now carries its own reason drawn from the ground the form prints beside it, all eleven boxes in that class are named in the guide in the form's own words, the sweep sentence is replaced by a counted statement generated from the dispositions, and six guards in the ORDINARY build path refuse the defect's return. Both fixture PDFs are byte-identical, so the acceptance receipt still binds and no raster is owed. The counter that should have caught this cannot: the shared reader does not read selection controls on this field-map shape at all.
actedOnReturns: VF61 rows-vf61-20260910.json, the verification that refused this family on ROUTE_OPTIONS at b984a2f843e493e855442fd25d3a4e73d01a0686. Its ROUTE_OPTIONS finding was re-measured from the committed bytes by this lane and reproduced in full. Its fourteen PASS obligations were NOT re-derived, as the grant directed.
FIX164 rows-fix164-20260910.json, the byte-free repair VF61 verified. Nothing FIX164 wrote was undone.
sharedManifestsTouched: None. RASTER_QUEUE.json, MASTER_QUEUE.json and both record-clearing manifests were READ and never modified. Nothing under data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/ other than fix172/ is in either commit. The claim ledger was touched by claim.mjs --release only and that edit is left UNCOMMITTED. The shared completeness verifier and completeness contract were READ and NOT modified -- see theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAREDCODE.

EXP102/EXP104/EXP106 resolve to private/source-imports/Nationwide_Recovery_Pool_2026-09-02/LegalEase Minnesota/, FEE102 to private/source-imports/rcap-d-source-packs-2026-08-12/. MASTER_LIBRARY_SOURCE_DIR was left at its default.
howBytesWereMeasured: sha256sum on the files as they sit on disk, before the first edit and after each build, and `sha256sum -c` against a pinned list after every mutation test. The printed face of EXP102 pages 4 and 5 was read back through the same shared anchor-capture path the census uses (extractTextItems + groupIntoLines + normalizeHarvestedText over pdf-lib's page objects) from the exact binary the family binds, sha256 c98430f1a9c7a6d399b7d01de1ef2eee0df5f0a1a07e89a703b307977d7bf541, so the ten reasons quote the form rather than a memory of it.

howTheOUTPUTWASPROTECTEDBEFORERUNNINGANY: This builder does NOT delete its output directory before rendering -- there is no rmSync anywhere in it, only mkdirSync({recursive:true}) and per-file writeFileSync -- so a failed build leaves the previous output in place. That was checked by reading the source before the first run, not assumed. A full copy of the family directory and of the builder was still taken to the scratchpad first, and `git checkout` remained the primary restore path throughout.

theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.whereItLives: scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/verify-packet-completeness.mjs, function readFieldRows, the 'anchors-and-withheld' branch (the shape this family's production-field-map.json uses).
theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.whatItReads: doc.writableAnchors and doc.withheld. It does NOT read doc.selectionControls at all on this shape.
theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.theARITHMETICTHATPROVESIT: The verifier reports '30/387 written' on this family. writableAnchors across the four documents are 19+3+4+4 = 30. withheld are 118+34+62+143 = 357. 30+357 = 387 exactly. This family declares 27+0+36+32 = 95 selection controls and NOT ONE of them is in the 387. So requiredOptionsMissing is structurally 0 here whatever these boxes carry, before any question about a null reason arises.
theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.theSECONDLAYER: Even if a selection control did reach classifyBlank in scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/completeness-contract.mjs, the declared not-applicable gate is entered on a NAMED routeConditionThatMakesItInapplicable and never inspects `reason`. A row can name a condition and say nothing about why the box is empty, and the gate passes it.
theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.whatTHISLANECHANGED: Nothing in either shared file. Both were read and left byte-identical. The scoped answer is a guard in this family's own build path that refuses to deliver a selection control with no stated reason, plus a published measurement at data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/mn/mn-petition-15218-set--official-pdf-fill/reports/selection-disclosure.json which states the shared reading beside its own and says in terms why the two are not measurements of the same thing.
theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.whatISSTILLOWEDANDBYWHOM: A shared-code lane should make readFieldRows read selectionControls on the anchors-and-withheld shape, and make the declared not-applicable gate require a reason as well as a condition. Until then requiredOptionsMissing cannot see this class of defect on ANY family using this field-map shape -- not only this one. This lane does not own those files and did not touch them.
theCOUNTERISBLINDANDTHEBLINDNESSISINSHAR.whyTHATNUMBERDIDNOTMOVEANDSHOULDNOTBEREA: It is the same blind 0 in both readings. The number that moved is in reports/selection-disclosure.json: selectionControlsWithNoStatedReason was 10 on the committed bytes and is 0 now, and the build refuses rather than ever delivering a non-zero one.

theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.sourceItRestsOn: EXP102 Rev 7/24 page 4, the second box under item 9 "Qualification for Expungement", printed lines y=572.0/555.2/540.0: "You were certified or referenced for prosecution as an adult for a crime you committed when you were a juvenile. [Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Record - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 1 or 2 (court form EXP106).]"
theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.reasonWritten: This box is EXP102 item 9's second ground: "You were certified or referenced for prosecution as an adult for a crime you committed when you were a juvenile." It is the one other ground on item 9 that uses the same proposed order this packet carries — the form prints "[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Record - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 1 or 2 (court form EXP106).]" under it — but it is a different petition, proved by different facts, and nothing in this packet was prepared or worded for a juvenile certification. Leave it empty here. If this is your ground and the § 152.18 discharge is not, ask for the packet built for it instead of adding this box to this one.

theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.sourceItRestsOn: EXP102 Rev 7/24 page 4, third box under item 9, printed lines y=516.0/499.2: "A criminal matter was resolved your favor. [Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105).]"
theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.reasonWritten: This box is EXP102 item 9's third ground: "A criminal matter was resolved your favor." The form sends that ground to a different proposed order — it prints "[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105).]" under it — and this packet carries EXP106, not EXP105. Ticking it here would ask the court for relief under a subdivision the order in your envelope does not cover. Leave it empty. If your case was resolved in your favour rather than dismissed and discharged under § 152.18, this is the wrong packet.

[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105).]"
theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.reasonWritten: This box is EXP102 item 9's fourth ground: "You successfully completed the terms of a diversion program or stay of adjudication, and you have not been charged with a new crime for at least one year since completion of the diversion program or stay of adjudication." A diversion or a stay of adjudication is not the same disposition as a § 152.18 discharge, and the form sends it to a different proposed order — "[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105).]" This packet carries EXP106. Leave it empty here.

theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.reasonWritten: This box is EXP102 item 9's fifth ground: "You were convicted of a petty misdemeanor or misdemeanor, or the sentence imposed was within the limits provided by law for a misdemeanor, and you have not been convicted of a new crime for at least two years since discharge of the sentence for the crime." It is a CONVICTION ground. The box this packet ticks is a case that was dismissed and discharged without a conviction, and the form sends a conviction to a different proposed order — "[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105).]" Leave it empty here.

This packet carries EXP106 and petitions on a discharge, not a conviction. Leave it empty here.

They are different grounds, they have different waiting periods, and the form sends this one to a different proposed order — "[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105)]." If you were convicted rather than discharged, this is the wrong packet.

theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.reasonWritten: This box is EXP102 item 9's tenth ground: "You were convicted of a felony violation of an offense listed in Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3(b), and have not been convicted of a new crime for at least four years since discharge of the sentence for the crime." Subdivision 3(b) is a named list of felonies that may be expunged after four years; whether your offence is on that list is a question about your own record, which this packet does not hold. The form sends this ground to "[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105)]." This packet carries EXP106. Leave it empty here.

[Use Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Order to Seal/Expunge Judicial Records Only (court form EXP107).]"
theTENREASONSANDWHERETHEYCAMEFROM.reasonWritten: This box is EXP102 item 9's eleventh ground: "You were convicted of an offense that does not qualify for expungement under Minn. Stat. § 609A.02, subd. 3, but you believe you have rehabilitated yourself. You believe that the benefit to you outweighs the disadvantage to the public and the burden on the court." It asks the court to seal its own file only: the form sends it to "[Use Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Order to Seal/Expunge Judicial Records Only (court form EXP107).]", which this packet does not carry, and which does not reach records held outside the courthouse. Leave it empty here.

whyNONEOFTHETENISTICKED: Each of the ten states a different statutory ground for expungement and a participant electing one is swearing to it under Minn. Stat. Sec 358.116. A raster is re-earnable; a pre-answered sworn election is not curable by disclosure. This repair adds no ink anywhere: both fixture PDFs are byte-identical to the committed ones.
